items.title: Thousands evacuate after Indonesia quake kills 51, cuts roads
items.summary: SIKKA: Around 5,000 people have been evacuated after a magnitude-7.7 earthquake smashed an area in eastern Indonesia, killing at least 51, blocking roads and causing landslides, authorities said on Sunday. Thirty-six people were seriously injured in the Saturday morning quake in East Nusa Tenggara province, while 77 had minor injuries, Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus told a televised meeting. More than 3,300 people in the Sikka region self-evacuated or were stranded in a sports arena, said the disaster mitigation agency BNPB.

items.title: Anwar launches Temu Fikrah, PKR Youth’s manifesto‑meets‑manual for courage, creativity and Madani governance
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched Temu Fikrah , a publication produced by the PKR Youth wing (AMK) in conjunction with the PKR National Congress 2026. The 113-page publication, authored by AMK chief Muhammad Kamil Ahmad Munim and AMK executive committee member Ashraf Ahmad Hadi, outlines the movement’s new thinking on addressing contemporary challenges. In the foreword, Anwar described the publication as timely, coinciding with the adoption of the Malaysia Madani concept as the intellectual framework and strategic direction for the nation’s administration.

items.title: DAP backs Anwar's plan to abolish AUKU, urges wider reforms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: DAP will give its full support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's proposal to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), while urging the government to apply the same momentum to other longstanding promises. Secretary-general Anthony Loke said the abolition of AUKU had been a cause championed by DAP for decades, describing the prime minister's announcement as a significant moment. "DAP will give him 100 per cent support.

items.title: Eastern Japan rain kills nine: Report
items.summary: TOKYO: Heavy rain that battered eastern Japan has left nine people dead, public broadcaster NHK said Sunday, after an "unprecedented" deluge that flooded over a thousand homes and snarled up roads and rail services. Torrential downpours starting late Thursday triggered landslide warnings and power outages, with forecasters issuing the highest-level heavy rain warning for the Chiba region for the first time. Over 70 houses across the Chiba region were partially destroyed by the rain, the prefecture's latest tally showed.

items.title: PKR’s 27‑year struggle isn’t about power, Zaliha says it’s about changing how Malaysia is run
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Becoming a government is not the end of the Reformasi struggle but rather a real test to prove the courage and wisdom to implement change, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa. She said the reformasi struggle led by PKR for 27 years should not be seen simply as an effort to take over the country’s administration, but rather aimed at changing the way the country is governed. “Implementing reform also requires wisdom.

items.title: Ramanan calls for unity among PKR leaders
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR leaders must stop attacking one another as internal disputes risk splitting the party at the grassroots and weakening its machinery, vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan warned today. Ramanan said conflicts among leaders at the top would eventually have repercussions on branches and members on the ground. Ramanan said party leaders and members must remember that no individual or personal interest was greater than PKR and its wider struggle.

items.title: GOF personnel injured as suspected migrant smuggler reverses car into him
items.summary: GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the 29-year-old corporal sustained injuries to his head, hands, body and knees in the 8.30pm incident. The driver was detained," he said. Ahmad Radzi said the 34-year-old driver, from Kampung Kenat Bunut Susu, had 15 previous criminal offences, including drug-related offences, vehicle theft and offences under the Penal Code and Immigration Act.

items.title: DAP’s destiny on the table as Anthony Loke leaves Unity decision to Putrajaya delegates
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — The DAP Party Conference today is the appropriate forum to decide whether the party should remain in or withdraw from the Unity Government, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke. Therefore, the delegates have to make a collective decision for the party. He said this when delivering his policy speech at the 2026 DAP Party Conference at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here.

items.title: Kelantan health authorities monitor newborn exposed to drugs in womb
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Health Department is monitoring a newborn girl who tested positive for amphetamines and benzodiazepines following a urine screening at the Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital (HRPZ II) Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) on Aug 6. Deputy health director Dr Rohana Daud said the mother was believed to have taken sedatives, prompting health officials to monitor the infant for withdrawal symptoms. However, health authorities will continue follow-up treatment to ensure the child's development is not affected," she said.

items.title: Loke apologises to DAP delegates for losing Chennah in Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today apologised to party delegates for failing to retain Chennah, a seat he had held for three consecutive terms since 2013, in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election. “I felt saddened that as the party secretary-general I was unable to retain the seat in the recent Negeri Sembilan state election and for that I would like to apologise to all the delegates for this defeat. In the recent Negeri Sembilan state election, Loke lost to MCA’s John Kong Choon, who won the seat with a majority of 688 votes.

items.title: Loke apologises to DAP delegates over Chennah defeat
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has apologised to party delegates over the loss of the Chennah state seat in the Negri Sembilan election. Addressing the party's National Congress at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre today, Loke said the defeat left him with "a deep sense of sadness." Loke said he contested the Malay-majority constituency to demonstrate that DAP could win support across communities.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi suspends MARA staff after eight students allege sexual harassment misconduct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) has immediately suspended a member of its staff following allegations of sexual harassment involving at least eight students at a MARA educational institution. MARA chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the action was taken to facilitate a thorough investigation to be conducted without interference from the parties involved. He said the matter came to light after receiving direct messages from several students claiming to be victims, prompting him to order MARA management to take immediate action.

items.title: New plans to underpin Maxis' mobile growth
items.summary: Its postpaid subscriptions rose 0.7 per cent and average revenue per user (ARPU) increased 0.3 per cent. Maxis' prepaid subscriptions grew 0.4 per cent QoQ, while ARPU rose 1.4 per cent. Home connections increased 0.7 per cent QoQ and 3.2 per cent YoY, while ARPU rose 0.6 per cent QoQ.

items.title: Loke tables motion at DAP national congress to decide whether party stays in Cabinet
items.summary: ss PUTRAJAYA: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke has tabled a motion at the party's national congress here for delegates to decide via secret ballot whether to remain in the Cabinet. He reminded delegates that DAP had been in the federal government for nearly three years and eight months — longer than its first stint in power in 2018. "The first time lasted only 22 months.

items.title: Doctor loses RM588,000 in Dungun Forex investment scam
items.summary: DUNGUN: A private doctor lost RM588,000 after she was allegedly duped by a Forex and Ethereum investment scheme promising lucrative returns, police said. Dungun district police chief Superintendent Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the victim was a 32-year-old who had seen an advertisement for trading or investment lessons on Instagram in January 2026. "The frightened victim made 77 transactions to six different bank accounts.

items.title: Sime Darby Property tops out first Elmina high-rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd has topped out Kanopi Residences, its first high-rise residential development in the 141.64-hectare Elmina City Centre in Sungai Buloh, Selangor. Located on Persiaran Garcinia near Elmina Lakeside Mall, Kanopi Residences is part of the 2630-hectare City of Elmina masterplan and targets young professionals, first-time homebuyers and starter families. [[nid:1512189]] Kanopi Residences is also located near several national and international schools.

items.title: PKR must focus on bread-and-butter issues, not just economic figures — Fahmi
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR must focus more on the economic pressures faced by ordinary Malaysians, as strong macroeconomic indicators alone may not be enough to win over voters, party information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Fahmi said indicators such as gross domestic product growth, unemployment, government revenue, trade and investment inflows reflected the broader strength of the economy, but did not necessarily translate into improvements felt by households. Fahmi said recent political developments showed that strong economic performance alone was not enough if voters continued to feel pressure in their daily lives.

items.title: Affin Hwang trims CelcomDigi earnings projection
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Affin Hwang Investment Bank Bhd has trimmed its earnings forecasts for CelcomDigi Bhd after factoring one-off adjustments incurred in the second quarter (Q2) of 2026. Affin Hwang cut the company's 2026-2028 earnings forecast by 0.1 per cent to 1.0 per cent The firm said the impact was partly cushioned by lower future losses from CelcomDigi's 33.3 per cent stake in Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB). CelcomDigi's first-half 2026 (6M26) core net profit slipped one per cent year-on-year to RM816 million, while service revenue increased 1.5 per cent to RM5.43 billion.

items.title: PKR must address public fears, concerns ahead of GE16, says Youth chief
items.summary: PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Munim said the time remaining before the 16th General Election was urgent and should be fully used by PKR leaders and members to fix existing weaknesses. Also present were PKR leaders, including party president and PH chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. "Historically, PKR creates a surprise every 10 years.

items.title: Failure to learn lessons of war is why US faces quagmire in Iran
items.summary: LETTER: United States President Donald Trump said after defeating Iran, the US would take over control of the Strait of Hormuz. Military theorist Carl Von Clausewitz famously wrote that war is the continuation of politics by other means insisting that military action is only a tool to achieve a rational political goal. The challenges include morale, logistical support, extreme weather and political interference with the military conduct of the war.

items.title: DAP backs Anwar ‘100 per cent’ on AUKU abolition, Loke says reforms must go further
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP today said it will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim “100 per cent” in abolishing the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU), but stressed that the same spirit must be extended to other promised reforms. DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said education reform should go beyond the abolition of AUKU and focus on ensuring equal access to higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background. “AUKU is one component, but what is more important in education reform is to ensure equal opportunities for higher education for all Malaysians, regardless of their racial background.

items.title: DAP calls for stronger economic and institutional reform
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to step up institutional and economic reforms, three and a half years into the unity government's term. Gobind said he and other DAP leaders had pressed Anwar to move faster on the reform agenda. "I have seen that recently, leaders from DAP, myself included, have asked that the Prime Minister look seriously at the economic reforms that can help the people," he said.

items.title: Malaysian pilot allegedly smuggled drugs abroad multiple times since 2024
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested with about 25 kilogrammes of drugs in Indonesia last month is believed to have smuggled illicit substances abroad multiple times since 2024. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the finding was based on interrogations conducted by NCID officers in Jakarta. Hussein said the pilot also disclosed details about several drug syndicates in Malaysia and other countries, including Indonesia.

items.title: Fadhlina tells PKR members not to wait for Parliament dissolution to prepare for polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek has urged party members to remain election-ready at all times and not wait for Parliament to be dissolved before making preparations. “We must strengthen PKR so that whoever is with us, we remain strong. Whoever leaves us, we remain strong.

items.title: Husband recalls wife's final day before fatal floodgate accident
items.summary: SABAK BERNAM: A 63-year-old security guard said he was deeply saddened at not being able to meet his wife before her tragic death due to his night-shift work over the past two days. Basar, a security guard at the Sabak Bernam District Education Office, said he was sleeping at home when his son-in-law called to inform him of the tragedy. The father of six children, aged between 23 and 36, said his wife was closing the floodgate due to high tide while accompanied by their second child.

items.title: Hainan free trade port to deepen cooperation with Malaysian, Asean ports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hainan is emerging as a key gateway between China and the global economy as it accelerates the development of its free trade port (FTP), with new opportunities spanning supply chains, digital trade, investment, tourism and education. These developments are explored in Bernama TV's upcoming special documentary, "2026: Towards The Hainan Free Trade Port", which offers an in-depth look at how Hainan is reshaping its economic landscape and strengthening its links with regional and international markets. "2026: Towards The Hainan Free Trade Port" will air on Bernama TV on Aug 18 at 8.30 pm.

items.title: Anthropic IPO valuation hinges on US$190-200bil 2028 revenue forecast
items.summary: NEW YORK: As Anthropic prepares for what could be one of the biggest initial public offerings (IPOs) on record, Wall Street is looking further into the future than it commonly does to put a price on the artificial intelligence (AI) company, valuing it based on how much revenue it could generate two years from now. Anthropic is projecting 2028 revenue of roughly US$190 billion to US$200 billion, according to two people familiar with the company's financials, a figure that has not previously been reported. The projection dwarfs the US$47 billion revenue "run rate", reflecting the firm's current pace of business, that the company publicised as recently as May, and shows the scale of growth investors are being asked to underwrite.

items.title: 'I'd ride around here to 'fly'': 5 'Supermen' held in DUKE racing crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "After work, I would ride around here to 'fly'." The boy, who no longer attends school, said he would ride around the area after finishing work at a burger stall. Zamzuri said the five were detained under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act for reckless and dangerous driving.

items.title: 'Who's next after Anwar?' Zaliha urges PKR to prepare future leaders
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR must begin preparing a new generation of leaders capable of succeeding Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and eventually leading the country, party vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa said today. Zaliha said the party could not afford to wait until Anwar decided to step down before asking who was ready to take over. She said that in the early years of PKR's struggle, one of its main objectives was to ensure Anwar became prime minister.

items.title: Mara suspends staff member over sexual harassment allegations involving eight students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) has immediately suspended a staff member following allegations of sexual harassment involving at least eight students at a Mara educational institution. Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the action was taken to facilitate a thorough investigation without interference from the parties involved. Asyraf Wajdi said Mara would never compromise on any form of misconduct and assured that no cases would be covered up to protect the institution's reputation.

items.title: Control the media? We even give them massage chairs, Fahmi tells PKR congress
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today suggested that PKR will not resort to punitive measures against members of the press, even as some in the party believe its rivals are winning the messaging battle by fighting dirty. Speaking to party delegates, Fahmi suggested that PKR had lost the communications war, leading voters to “vote over emotions instead of performance”. Fahmi said instead that his party was treating the press much better than previous governments, joking that it even provided massage chairs to reporters covering the party’s congress.

items.title: Fadhlina: PKR must remain strong regardless of who stays or leaves
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR must build enough strength to remain resilient regardless of shifts in political alliances or who chooses to stay in or leave the Unity Government, its Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek said today. Whoever leaves us, we remain strong," she said. Fadhlina said PKR valued sincere partners and respected political cooperation, but must continue developing its organisational strength to safeguard the reform agenda.

items.title: RM12bil-RM14bil infrastructure contracts set for second half awards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Public infrastructure projects worth an estimated RM12 billion-RM14 billion are expected to be awarded in the second half of 2026, giving construction companies a fresh pipeline of work, according to MBSB Research. The firm said the projects would provide a fresh pipeline for construction companies, as data centre developments continue to drive private-sector growth. "Meanwhile, Langat 2 Phase 2, estimated at RM3 billion to RM4 billion, has entered the procurement stage following pre-qualification for Packages 1 and 2, while Sungai Rasau Phase 2, worth an estimated RM2 billion to RM3 billion, could provide further water-related packages, " he said in a research note.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain expected in parts of Peninsula, Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas across Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak until 1pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) in a warning issued at 8.35am said the affected areas in the Peninsula include the whole of Perlis and Melaka, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu and Kota Setar in Kedah. In Sarawak, the affected areas include Mukah, Selangau, Sibu, Sarikei, Meradong, Bintulu, Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Subis in Miri.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms, heavy rain, strong winds in Perlis, Melaka, Sarawak, other areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit several areas in the Peninsula and Sarawak until 1pm today. The weather warning also involves Kuantan, Pekan and Jerantut in Pahang; Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor; Port Dickson, Seremban, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin in Negeri Sembilan; and Tangkak and Muar in Johor. For Sarawak, the same forecast was issued for the areas of Mukah, Selangau, Sibu, Sarikei, Maradong, Bintulu, Kapit, Bukit Mabong and Subis in Miri.

items.title: Civil service integrity showing positive trend, says Chief Secretary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Integrity among civil servants is showing a positive trend following various government initiatives to strengthen ethical values and empower the public service. Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar said initiatives such as the Integrity and Governance Award (AIGA) had produced encouraging results. "We introduced these initiatives to strengthen integrity among civil servants.

items.title: Community, private sector support vital for former Nada clients
items.summary: Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the lack of post-rehabilitation support, including difficulties securing jobs and social stigma, could undermine their confidence and hinder reintegration into society. He said vocational training at the Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen), coupled with support after release, could help clients rebuild their confidence and regain their footing. "Clients in Puspen will eventually leave.

items.title: Fahmi: PKR will improve communications, not control the media
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR will improve its communication strategy but will not resort to controlling the media, says party information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said the party acknowledged concerns raised during the 2026 PKR National Congress and would make adjustments to improve how information is communicated to the public. He said where inaccurate information emerged, the approach would instead be to engage media organisations in an orderly and respectful manner.

items.title: Teacher arrested over alleged sexual assault of Form Four student
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police received a report from the student on Aug 12 at 4.04pm. He said the student stated in the report that a male teacher had sexually assaulted the student at the school on Aug 10 at 10.15am. "On Aug 13 at 11.10am, police arrested the suspect, who teaches at the school attended by the victim," he said.

items.title: Rafizi: Bersama names 15 candidates early to give Melaka voters time to assess
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has announced candidates for 15 of the 28 seats in the Melaka state legislative assembly, becoming the first party to unveil its candidates ahead of the state election, The Star reported. The party’s line-up includes Dr Muhamad Solehin Saleh, 40, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, who will contest Bemban. Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said the early announcement was made before the state assembly is dissolved, allowing voters more time to assess the candidates and their plans.

items.title: PAS wants Selangor to be launchpad for toppling PH, says Sanusi
items.summary: “If PH falls in Selangor, PH will fall at the federal level,” he was quoted as saying at a Selangor PAS election machinery gathering at the Selangor PAS complex here last night. What has PH achieved? PH and BN subsequently formed the state government.

items.title: Student loses RM29,000 after scammers pose as cops, threaten arrest over money laundering
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 16 — Police arrested three local men, aged between 32 and 45, in five raids across Kuala Lumpur and Selangor on Thursday for allegedly being involved in an online scam syndicate. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects were arrested at various locations in Petaling Jaya, Kelana Jaya, Ulu Kelang, Damansara and Kuala Lumpur. He said the arrests followed a police report lodged by a 22-year-old student who lost RM28,999 after being deceived by individuals posing as law enforcement officers and claiming that he was involved in money laundering.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin graces Perak Merdeka Month programme with 214,095 student entries
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 16 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today graced a programme to instil the spirit of loyalty to the Ruler and country in conjunction with the Perak-level 2026 Merdeka Month at Bangunan Perak Darul Ridzuan here last night. Also in attendance were the Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim, accompanied by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh. Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar, in his royal address, said this year’s programme recorded an encouraging turnout, with 214,095 entries involving 83.6 per cent of primary and secondary school students in Perak.

items.title: ESSCom chief: Claims of armed men entering Semporna, Lahad Datu baseless
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Claims of a group of armed men entering Semporna and Lahad Datu, Sabah that went viral on social media are fake, Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) commander Datuk Victor Sanjos said. Victor said ESSCom always monitors and implements security control, especially in waters and strategic locations in the East Sabah Security Zone, adding that any information about security threats should be channelled to the authorities for further action and confirmation. — Bernama

items.title: Police probe Facebook account owner over alleged seditious, insulting post against royals, govt
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 15 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is conducting an investigation into the owner of the Facebook account ‘Ahmad Mu’min’ following a post, which is suspected to contain elements of sedition and insult against the royal institution, the Malaysian government and the PDRM. Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 is being conducted after a report was received from a 29-year-old man at 11.14 am yesterday. “The police will investigate the identity of the account owner and subsequently conduct an investigation according to legal procedures,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Two drivers detained for allegedly blocking traffic to give way to supercar convoy
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Aug 16 — Police have detained two car drivers believed to have acted as “marshals” by obstructing traffic to give way to a luxury car convoy at Bulatan Lebuh Kota Iskandar here. Iskandar Puteri deputy police chief Supt Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the two men were arrested yesterday by the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division. “Acting on a public complaint, the Iskandar Puteri District Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division conducted an operation to trace the individuals involved.

items.title: Ramanan: PTPK financing may be converted from loans to grants
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — The Ministry of Human Resources (Kesuma) is seeking feedback and views from other ministries on its proposal to convert Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) financing from loans to grants. Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan said the views gathered would be presented to the Cabinet soon for consideration. Earlier at the programme, Ramanan said Kesuma, through Perkeso, had introduced MYFutureJobs Ambassador among higher education institution (IPT) students to increase awareness of career opportunities and MYFutureJobs services within campus communities.

items.title: Menu Rahmah operators nationwide reach 3,210 as of July, says deputy minister
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — A total of 3,210 food and beverage premises nationwide have registered as Menu Rahmah operators as of July this year, says Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Deputy Minister Datuk Fuziah Salleh. The highest participation, she said, was recorded among food stall or food court operators, with 1,016 registrations, besides restaurants, hawkers, food trucks and bazaars. She said the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) would continue to strengthen the promotion of Menu Rahmah through the ‘Jom Cari Menu Rahmah’ programme, besides working with more industry players, traders’ associations and food operators to expand the menu options to more locations.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul: Reform struggle must deliver tangible results for people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The reform struggle must be translated into results that can be seen and felt by the people, said Prime Minister’s Senior Political Advisor Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. The nation’s economy grew by six percent, outperforming all forecasts, but we must ensure the people reap the benefits,” he said via a Facebook post yesterday. Tengku Zafrul said communication efforts also need to be enhanced so that the people are aware of the various initiatives and achievements of the Madani Government.

items.title: Penang CM: State remains under control after North Sumatra earthquake tremors
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — The situation in Penang remains under control, with no injuries reported as of early today, following tremors felt across the state after an earthquake struck North Sumatra, Indonesia, yesterday. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government received reports from the Operations Centre of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) regarding the tremors. “The Operations Centre received calls from members of the public between 7.23 pm and 7.27 pm (yesterday) reporting tremors at nine locations across all five districts in Penang.

items.title: Northern Sumatra earthquake sends tremors across parts of Peninsular Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — A 6.4 magnitude earthquake hit northern Sumatra, Indonesia, at 6.54 pm yesterday, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said. MetMalaysia said the earthquake was centred at coordinates 2.9 degrees north and 98.8 degrees east, at a depth of 154 kilometres (km), 37 km southwest of Pematangsiantar. Meanwhile in Penang, Fire and Rescue Department director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said the department received nine emergency calls regarding the tremors at around 6.55 pm.

items.title: From rice to remedy: Penang maker’s time‑honoured 40‑day method keeps traditional ‘bedak sejuk’ craft alive
items.summary: Over the years, however, bedak sejuk gradually fell out of favour, often regarded as an old-fashioned product used mainly by older generations. But in recent years, traditional bedak sejuk has begun to regain popularity, helped by greater public interest in heritage products, according to maker Yeoh Siong Huat. Yeoh said his parents had previously operated a small-scale business rearing pigs while also producing belacan and bedak sejuk for sale.

items.title: Fire dept calls for systematic measures to prevent fallen tree incidents nationwide
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Incidents of fallen trees in Malaysia can no longer be considered isolated incidents that only occur during the rainy season; instead, they require a preventive approach that is more systematic through regular safety audits, inter-agency data sharing and consistent maintenance. Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) statistics show that 26,001 cases of fallen trees were recorded nationwide from 2021 to June, last year, resulting in 50 fatalities and 243 injuries. Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said that emergency calls related to fallen trees remain consistently high, ranging between 4,400 and 5,200 cases per year, while for the first half of 2026 alone, 1,912 cases were recorded.

items.title: Sabah teacher uses Jawi to bridge cultural and religious differences in Beluran
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — For Lorenica Frenila Masundim, teaching Jawi script at a school in Sabah’s interior is more than a lesson in writing, it is a way of bringing students and the wider community closer while fostering understanding across racial, religious and cultural differences. Lorenica said she found great fulfilment in seeing non-Muslim students who were once unfamiliar with Jawi gradually learn to read and understand their function as part of the Malay writing system. Lorenica was first introduced to the Jawi script in 2009 when she took the Basic Introduction to Jawi Writing course for one semester at the Institute of Teacher Education, Gaya Campus in Kota Kinabalu.

items.title: Sabah leaders’ presence at PKR congress reflects strong ties, cooperation, says Mustapha
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, and other leaders’ attendance at the 2026 PKR National Congress today reflects the strong ties and spirit of cooperation between Sabah and federal governments. Sabah PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the cooperation extended beyond politics, encompassing all aspects. Among the GRS leaders present were Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Sabah Rural Development Minister Datuk Rubin Balang and Sabah Youth, Sports Development and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan.

items.title: Auditor-general: Audit reports key to strengthening accountability, transparency and governance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The National Audit Department (JAN) is carrying out its mandate as the country’s audit institution independently, professionally and with integrity in strengthening accountability, transparency and governance in the public sector, says Auditor General Datuk Seri Wan Suraya Wan Mohd Radzi. She said audit findings were translated into the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN), which is one of the important instruments in the country’s checks-and-balances mechanism. She said the Auditor General’s firmness in providing opinions on Financial Statements and making audit recommendations was not merely to fulfil reporting requirements to Parliament, but more importantly, to encourage effective corrective action and improvements in public sector management.

items.title: On-demand car sharing platform, Socar is shutting down in Malaysia after 8 years of operations.
items.summary: Effective today, the Socar app will no longer accept Wallet top-ups and new monthly pass subscriptions. However, take note that only Socar will cease operations as its peer-to-peer service, Trevo, is still available in Malaysia. Unlike Socar which essentially works like an on-demand car rental service, Trevo is essentially an “Airbnb” of sorts for car sharing.

items.title: Fahmi: PKR to strengthen communication strategy to better convey govt messages
items.summary: PKR Information Chief, who is also Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, said the move followed several proposals raised by delegates at the ongoing PKR National Congress 2026 at the Melaka International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITC), Ayer Keroh. “This is important (to strengthen information dissemination and communication). Fahmi said several views and planned changes related to information dissemination and communication proposals would be presented during the winding-up session tomorrow.

items.title: PKR Selangor delegate calls for party to use own logo in Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — A Selangor PKR delegate today proposed that the party return to using its own logo in future elections, starting with the upcoming Melaka state election. Ahmad Danish Hairudin, who is also PKR national Youth information chief, said it was timely for the party to campaign under its own logo in the state polls. PKR has used its iconic blue-and-white logo in several elections.

items.title: Subang airport runway reopens after helicopter explosion, eight flights diverted
items.summary: SUBANG, Aug 15 — The runway at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here has been reopened after being temporarily closed following a helicopter exploding and catching fire during an engine run-up test earlier this afternoon. Malaysian Civil Aviation Authority (CAAM) chief executive officer Capt Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the incident occurred at Taxiway Victor, leading to a temporary suspension of flights. Norazman said during the runway closure, eight inbound flights were diverted to other airports, while three departing flights had to be delayed.
